note: cdn_ui is the admin UI submodule for CDN. It has no config of its own; it edits cdn.settings. Easy cases cover its route/permission/target config. Medium/hard cases are grounded in the cdn.settings values the UI form writes (status, mapping.domain, farfuture.status) — the end state a UI save produces — and only touch local config. Baseline restored explicitly by cleanup/reset.

evals.prompt: The Drupal cdn module has no settings page of its own. Its cdn_ui submodule adds one. What is the admin path of that CDN settings form, and which permission controls access to it?
evals.expected_output: The form is at /admin/config/services/cdn (route cdn_ui.settings) and is gated by the 'administer CDN configuration' permission.

evals.prompt: When I save the CDN UI settings form, which configuration object does it actually write to?
evals.expected_output: It writes cdn.settings (the config object owned by the cdn module). cdn_ui has no config of its own.

evals.prompt: After I finish configuring the CDN through the CDN UI submodule, can I uninstall CDN UI without losing my CDN configuration? Why?
evals.expected_output: Yes. CDN UI stores no configuration of its own — it only edits cdn.settings — so uninstalling it leaves the CDN configuration intact and the cdn module keeps working.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the CDN has been configured through the admin UI. Inspect the live configuration and tell me the CDN domain that the CDN UI Mapping tab currently shows.
On this Drupal site, inspect the CDN configuration that the CDN UI manages and tell me which URL scheme is currently configured for CDN file URLs.

On this Drupal site, use the CDN configuration (as the CDN UI settings form would) to turn CDN serving ON and set the CDN domain to cdn-ui-hard.example.com with a simple mapping. Apply the change to the live configuration.
On this Drupal site, turn OFF the CDN module's 'Far Future' forever-cacheable file serving in configuration. Apply the change to the live configuration.
